# SPD-050 — Stop hook: a spudagent resumed with SendMessage after its return still counts as returned, so Law 9 asks Spud to finish a running member

## Brief
A spudagent resumed with SendMessage after it returns keeps its returned state in the ledger, so Spud's Stop hook holds the turn with Law 9 and tells him to `member finish` a member that is running again. Recording it at that moment would write an outcome for work still in progress. Observed on SPD-046: Sieglinde (01) returned at 10:54 and her SubagentStop was recorded. Spud resumed her by agent id with SendMessage for a round-2 re-brief, which replied "Resuming agent" and recorded `member edit --brief`. At the end of that turn Stop held, naming her "stopped 2026-09-14T10:54" and unrecorded, while ListAgents showed the same agent running.

Find out what the harness gives the hooks when a subagent is resumed: whether SubagentStart fires again with the same agent_id, whether a PreToolUse or PostToolUse event names SendMessage, or whether only the member's next tool call shows it alive. Then make a resumed member count as live again (clear or supersede its return, perhaps with a `member.resumed` event), so Stop holds only once it returns a second time and SubagentStop's checks apply to the new return. If the harness offers no signal, a `spud member resume <ref>` command Spud runs before SendMessage is the fallback, and CLAUDE.md's protocol gets a line for it. Tests in tests/test_hooks.py.
